title: Protocol to assess retinal metabolic flux of mice via stable isotope-resolved metabolomics
author: Komissarov, Pandey, et al.

steps.title: Prepare 50 µM metabolite standard mix
steps.instruction: Dissolve the solid metabolites listed in Table 1 in HPLC‑grade water to make a 50 µM solution (50 µM of each metabolite). Aliquot and dry the solution, then store the dried aliquots at –80 °C. (Metabolic analysis preparation timing: 3–4 h)

steps.title: Prepare extraction buffer, standards, and internal standard
steps.instruction: On a metal block placed on dry ice, thaw the dried standard mix. Pipette 20, 10, 4, 2, and 0.4 µL of the standard mix into separate 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes to generate a standard curve of 0, 0.02, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, and 1 nmol of each metabolite. Prepare a 10 mM methylsuccinate solution by adding 1.3211 mg methylsuccinate to 1 mL HPLC‑grade water; aliquot and store at –20 °C (6 months) or –80 °C (1 year). Make extraction buffer (150 µL per sample) using the example recipe: 10 µL of the 10 mM methylsuccinate, 8 mL methanol (HPLC‑grade), and 1.99 mL HPLC‑grade water to give 10 mL total. Cool the buffer on dry ice before use and keep it ice‑cold; use an acclimated pipette tip and keep samples on dry ice until homogenization.

substeps.instruction: Place a bucket of dry ice and set a metal block on it.
Remove samples and standard mix from –80 °C and place on the metal block.
Prepare 10 mM methylsuccinate (1.3211 mg in 1 mL water).
Prepare 150 µL extraction buffer per sample (example: 10 µL 10 mM methylsuccinate + 8 mL methanol + 1.99 mL water).
Cool the buffer on dry ice; keep it chilled and use ice‑cold pipette tips.

steps.title: Prepare methoxyamine‑HCl solution in pyridine
steps.instruction: Make a 20 mg/mL methoxyamine‑HCl solution in pyridine (e.g., dissolve 10 mg methoxyamine‑HCl in 500 µL pyridine). Mix with a rotating mixer until fully dissolved. Prepare 10 µL of this solution for each sample immediately before use; do not store or reuse.

steps.title: Generate SIM mass‑spec method
steps.instruction: Using the standards, create a selected‑ion monitoring (SIM) method that verifies the retention times and masses listed in Table 1 for routine analysis. Adjust parameters if using a different chromatography type (GC vs. LC) or column.

steps.title: Install required data‑analysis software
steps.instruction: Download and verify functionality of Agilent MSD ChemStation and Isocor (v1.0) for downstream data processing.

steps.title: Dissect retinal and RPE‑choroid tissue
steps.instruction: Euthanize the mouse by awake cervical dislocation, enucleate both eyes, and place them in a petri dish containing 5 mL HBSS at room temperature. Using Cohan‑Vannas spring scissors, forceps, and fine forceps, trim away fat, connective tissue, and muscle, then dissect out the neuroretina and RPE‑choroid. Avoid cutting through the eyecup or neuroretina and grasp near the optic nerve base to minimize connective tissue. (Incubation timing: 20–25 min per eyeball, can be overlapped).

steps.title: Wash tissue and perform 12C/13C incubations
steps.instruction: For each dissected tissue piece, perform the following sequence:

substeps.instruction: a. Quick dip and swirl the tissue in HBSS (wash).
b. Incubate the tissue in a 12C‑glucose well for 15 min at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.
c. Wash the tissue again in HBSS.
d. Incubate the tissue in a 13C‑glucose well for either 30 s or 90 s (experimental group) at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.
e. Wash the tissue in HBSS a final time.
f. Repeat steps a–e for each tissue sample, staggering samples as needed.

steps.title: Snap‑freeze tissue after final wash
steps.instruction: Place the washed tissue into a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube and snap‑freeze it in liquid nitrogen. Rinse forceps before the next dissection to avoid cross‑contamination. Store the frozen tissue at –80 °C (up to 12 months) until extraction.

steps.title: Thaw standards and samples on dry ice
steps.instruction: Remove the dried standard mix aliquots and the frozen tissue samples from –80 °C and place them on dry ice to thaw.

steps.title: Add ice‑cold extraction buffer
steps.instruction: Pipette 150 µL of the ice‑cold extraction buffer onto each thawed sample and each standard‑curve dilution. Keep all tubes on dry ice during this step.

substeps.instruction: a. Homogenize with a probe sonicator: 10 cycles at power setting 2 and 90 % duty cycle (RPE/Choroid).
b. Precipitate proteins by incubating the tubes on dry ice for 45 min.
c. Centrifuge at 17,000 × g for 30 min at 4 °C.
d. Transfer the clear supernatant to a new tube (pellet contains protein).
e. Dry the supernatant in a SpeedVac (typically 2–3 h) until completely dry.
f. Store the dried extracts and standard dilutions at –80 °C until further processing.

description: Changes to retinal cellular metabolism are an emerging hallmark associated with retinal dystrophies such as retinitis pigmentosa. Isotope tracing and metabolomics have made pinpointing the potential sites of dysfunction more accessible than ever. The following protocol describes the steps for analyzing glycolytic and TCA cycle activity in retinal-degenerate mouse retina and RPE-choroid tissue.1 Similar protocols can and have been adapted for use in other tissues and cells. For other metabolic processes, some redesigning has to be done with regard to which isotope-labeled metabolite is used for tissue incubation, as well as which metabolites to help analyze the metabolic pathway of interest. All animal experiments were conducted as approved by the Columbia University Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee. This protocol utilizes a 37°C incubator with 5% CO2 for tissue incubations.
